gloss: New Year's rice cake offering; mirror rice cake

definitions.explanation: A traditional Japanese New Year decoration consisting of two round rice cakes stacked on top of each other, often topped with a bitter orange (daidai). Displayed as an offering to the gods during the New Year period.

notes:
A key element of Japanese New Year (⟦{正月|しょうがつ}→正月：01433_shougatsu⟧) traditions. The name comes from ⟦{鏡|かがみ}→鏡：02190_kagami⟧ (mirror) because the round, flat shape resembles ancient bronze mirrors, which were considered sacred objects. The two stacked mochi represent the old and new years, or yin and yang.

CULTURAL NOTE:
Displayed from around December 28 until ⟦{鏡開|かがみびら}き→鏡開き：25599_kagamibiraki⟧ (January 11 in most regions), when the mochi is broken open (never cut with a knife, as cutting is considered unlucky) and eaten. Modern versions sold in supermarkets are often plastic containers shaped like {鏡餅|かがみもち} with individually wrapped mochi inside.
